surface_expression: The bowl is empty and the creature sits back on its haunches. Its belly is round and its eyes are half-closed.
It lies on its side with one paw stretched forward. A slow breath lifts the fur along its ribs.
The creature sleeps curled in a tight circle. Its nose is tucked beneath its tail and its breathing is even.
It presses its head against your hand and holds still. The warmth of its skull fills your palm.
The coat lies flat and glossy from ear to tail. Each strand catches the light when it turns.
You fill the bowl from the bag and set it on the stone floor. The sound of dry food hitting ceramic brings the creature running.
You hold the treat between two fingers and wait. The creature takes it gently and carries it to its corner.
You pour water into the dish until it catches the light. The creature drinks without lifting its head.
You toss the ball across the garden in a low arc. The creature is already moving before it leaves your hand.
You grip one end of the rope and brace. The creature digs in and pulls with a low growl that is not anger.
You scratch beneath the chin where the fur is softest. The creature tilts its head and closes its eyes.
You draw the brush from shoulder to haunch in long strokes. Loose fur gathers on the bristles and the creature leans into the pull.
You lift each paw and wipe the mud from between the pads. The creature holds still and watches your hands.
You turn the lamp down until only a glow remains. The creature settles deeper into its bed.
You hum a low melody without words. The creature's ears rotate forward and its breathing slows.
You unlatch the door and the light falls in a rectangle on the floor. The creature stands in the doorway and lifts its nose.
You fold the blanket once and drape it over the sleeping form. The creature shifts without waking.
The tail moves in wide sweeps that rock its entire back half. Its mouth is open and its tongue hangs to the left.
It exhales through its nose and rests its chin on its paws. The eyes remain open but unfocused.
All four feet leave the ground at once. It spins once and faces you with its weight forward.
A thin sound comes from behind closed teeth. The creature looks at the bowl and back at you.
Each blink takes longer than the last. The head dips and catches itself twice before settling.
The nose works in quick pulses, reading the air in layers. One ear turns toward the sound the other has already tracked.
It walks from door to window and back without stopping. Its nails click on the floor in a broken rhythm.
The front end drops while the back stays high. The tail vibrates and the eyes lock on the toy.
It leans its full weight against your leg and does not move. You feel its ribs expand with each breath.
It carries the stick high and trots with exaggerated steps. It will not put it down until you notice.
The den is a hollow of blankets in the corner of the room. The walls are warm and the light is filtered.
The garden is small and walled with stone. Sun falls on the grass in a shifting pattern through the leaves.
The kitchen corner holds two bowls on a mat. The stone floor is cool and the creature's nails tap on it.
The hearth holds a low fire that pops and settles. The creature lies as close as the heat allows.
The path runs along the fence and collects rain. Paw prints overlap in the soft ground.
The basin sits on a low stand with a folded towel beside it. Warm water steams in the morning air.
The front step overlooks the lane and catches the morning light. The creature sits here and watches everything pass.
The bed is raised off the floor and lined with wool. A dip in the centre marks where the creature sleeps.
Rain strikes the windows in gusts and the garden is grey. The creature watches from the doorway but does not go out.
Sunlight moves across the floor in a slow band. The creature follows it and lies in each new patch.
A breeze comes through the open window and lifts the curtain edge. The creature's nose twitches and its ears prick.
The house is still and the only sound is the clock. The creature's breathing is the loudest thing in the room.
A knock comes at the door and the creature is on its feet. Its ears are forward and its tail begins to move.
Snow falls past the window in slow diagonal lines. The creature presses its nose to the cold glass.
The door is open and the air smells of cut grass and distance. The creature stands at the threshold with its weight forward.
A low rumble crosses the sky and the windows rattle. The creature moves to the nearest person and presses close.
Birds call from the garden wall in short repeating phrases. The creature's head tracks left and right, calculating distance.
The fire has burned down to embers that pulse orange and grey. The creature's fur glows along the edges.
The ceramic bowl sits on the mat with a chip on the rim. The inside is worn smooth from use.
The water dish is heavy stoneware and holds a day's supply. A single hair floats on the surface.
The ball is red and has lost its bounce on one side. The creature finds it under furniture by smell.
The rope is braided cotton with two knots at each end. The middle section is damp and frayed from pulling.
The blanket is wool and carries the creature's scent. One corner is darker from being chewed.
The brush has natural bristles set in a wooden back. Loose fur clings between the rows.
The bone is dried and pale and fits in one paw. It is carried from room to room and hidden in blankets.
The collar is leather with a brass buckle. The inside is smooth from wear and the tag is scratched.
The bell is the size of a thimble and hangs from a loop. It rings when the creature runs.
The stick is hard and flavoured with something the creature favours. One end is splintered to a point.
The towel is folded on the basin edge and still warm. It smells of soap and clean water.
The duck is yellow rubber and makes a sound when bitten. The creature carries it everywhere after rain.
The pillow is dented in the centre where the creature curls. A ring of shed fur marks the edge.
A small sound comes from the creature's middle. It looks toward the kitchen and then at you.
It cannot settle in any position for more than a minute. The tail swishes low and the eyes are wide.
A single high note hangs in the room after you leave. It fades and comes again at intervals.
The back leg pumps against the shoulder in rapid bursts. The creature stops and starts and cannot quite reach.
The mouth opens wide enough to show every tooth. The front legs extend and the spine drops in a long curve.
It pushes the ball toward your foot with its nose. When you look down it steps back and waits.
A brown dog appears at the garden gate and stands with its tail level. The two sniff each other through the bars.
A sparrow lands on the windowsill and hops twice. The creature watches without moving, only its eyes tracking.
A child kneels on the floor and holds out both hands. The creature approaches low and then licks once.
The cat sits on the hearth rug with its paws tucked. The creature lies beside it without touching.
The mail carrier opens the gate and the creature runs to meet her. She leans down and scratches behind the ear.
Light enters the room from the east and moves across the floor. The creature stirs and stretches before opening its eyes.
The sun is directly overhead and the house is warm. The creature lies flat on the cool stone.
The light turns amber and the shadows stretch long. The creature sits at the window and watches the lane.
The sky dims and the lamps are not yet lit. The creature moves to its bed and circles twice.
The house is dark and the only sound is breathing. The creature sleeps and its paws twitch in a dream.
You open your eyes and the creature is already watching. It has been waiting without making a sound.
You set the bowl down and step back. The creature approaches and eats without rushing.
The collar clicks shut and the door opens. The creature steps out and the whole body lifts with anticipation.
The bowl is empty and the creature keeps checking. It sits by the mat and looks at you with increasing urgency.
It sighs — actually sighs — and drops its chin onto its paws. The toy is right there but the toy is not enough.
The eyes are heavy and the body lists to one side. It has been awake longer than it should.
It sits by the door and stares at the gap beneath. Every sound from outside makes the ears lift and fall.
The fur sticks out at odd angles behind the ears. The creature scratches and makes it worse.
The bin is on its side and the contents are sorted by interest. The creature sits among wrappers with no remorse.
Your left shoe has a new ventilation hole. The creature greets you with the lace still hanging from its mouth.
It returns from the garden wearing the garden. The tail wags as if this is an achievement.
Your sock is now a prize. The creature runs in tight circles with it, daring you to try.
Two paws on the counter and a nose in the butter dish. The creature freezes when caught, one paw still raised.
A hole has appeared where the tulips were. The creature's nose is black and its expression is innocent.
It stands at the window barking at something only it can see. The barking stops and starts without reason.
The toilet roll has been unspooled across the hallway. The creature sits at one end like a conquering general.
It sits in front of the empty bowl and does not move. The stare is patient and infinite.
The creature lies flat on its side and exhales with its whole body. This is the sigh of a creature that has known better days.
It has not moved from the door in twenty minutes. Every car that passes gets a head tilt and a tiny whine.
The back leg works at the shoulder in a blur. Something itches and nothing will fix it.
It walks from bed to door to bowl to bed again. Nothing is right and everywhere is wrong.
Chin on paws, eyes open, looking at nothing. The creature has decided to be sad and commits to it fully.
It sits perfectly still and aims both eyes at your plate. The ears are forward and the mouth is slightly open.
Something snaps and the creature runs at full speed in a perfect circle. The eyes are wild and the tongue flies sideways.
It will not look directly at you. The tail wags low and the whole body curves into an apology.
One sharp bark, then silence, then another. It is requesting your presence and will not stop.
It has turned its back to the room and pressed its nose into the corner. This is a protest.
At two in the morning the creature discovers urgent business. The sound of galloping fills the dark house.
The house is empty and the creature knows it. The settling sounds take on a different quality when no one is listening.
The collar hangs on its hook and the lead is coiled. The creature looks from one to the other and back to you.
The clock has passed the usual time and no bowl has appeared. The creature positions itself near the bag of food.
The ball sits in the middle of the floor, untossed. The creature has brought it three times and you have not noticed.
A crust of yesterday's food lines the bowl edge. The creature sniffs it and walks away.
After being fed it comes to find you and licks your hand once. The message is received.
The bowl is clean and the creature falls sideways onto the rug. The belly is round and the eyes are closing.
After the scolding and the cleanup, the tail begins again. The grudge lasted four seconds.
The coat lies smooth after the brush. The creature shakes once and struts as if wearing new clothes.
After the walk, the meal, and the chin scratch, the creature sleeps with a depth that says everything is right.
